translation: It enters to connect the brain, and again separately descends from the brain along the neck, runs along the scapula, and meets the Hand and Foot Taiyang and Shaoyang at Dazhu (BL11), below the first vertebra on both sides, one and a half cun from the midline of the spine in the hollow; internally it flanks the spine and reaches the waist, enters and runs along the u膂u (back muscles) to connect the kidney. The Nanjing says: The Du and Ren vessels are four chi five cun each, together nine chi in all. The Lingshu Jing says: The vessel in the center of the neck is the Du vessel, named Fengfu (GV16).
